notes: Destructive - the source file is gone after the merge and this cannot be undone.
Both lookups must resolve to exactly one file; no match or more than one match is an error (IR-4001) and the merge step is never reached. The user is not asked to pick.
The request body of the merge call is just the target file id as a bare JSON number.

The merge step is a destructive write, so the standard write policy applies - previewed under writeMode dry-run (nothing is sent), blocked under deny, sent under allow; and because it is destructive it also needs explicit confirmation (confirm=<previewId> from a prior preview, while requireConfirm is on, the default).
The merge call returns no body, so the flow outputs the id of the target file (from step 2); fetch the file again to see its merged content.

steps.onError: No match is an error, not a question - the flow stops with IR-4001 (ObjectNotFound, "no file has number <sourceFileNumber>") and nothing is merged. More than one match is also an error - the flow stops with IR-4001 ("file number <sourceFileNumber> matches more than one file") rather than guessing which file to merge away.

output.select: the single match; its Id is the source file

notes: Both lookups must resolve to exactly one file; no match or more than one match is an error (IR-4001) and no document is transferred. The user is not asked to pick.

Documents always live under a folder, never directly in a file. The documents go into the folder of the target file whose description is targetFolderName; no match or more than one match is an error (IR-4001) and nothing is transferred. The source side is not narrowed by folder.
The source file is never deleted. Move mode relocates its documents and leaves the file empty; copy mode leaves it untouched.

Exactly one of steps 5 and 6 runs, chosen by mode, so exactly one of moveResult (DocumentMoveResult) and copyResult (DocumentActionResult) is set. Both carry DocumentIdMap and PageIdMap (old id to new id).
Copying only exists in REST v2 (POST /api/v2/documents/copy); there is no v1 copy call. Moving uses the v1 call, with POST /api/v2/documents/move as the version alternative.
The copy step leaves CopyOption out, so the server's default copy kind applies (Logical reference or physical copy). Validation needed - that default is unconfirmed.

Validation needed - document type matching is by type code, not name, but a found document only carries DocumentTypeId and DocumentTypeDescription. Turning codes into DocumentTypeIds (e.g. from GET /api/objecttypes/{standardObjectClass} with Document) and filtering on those is a likely route, but it is unconfirmed which object type field holds the code.

The move or copy step is a write, so the standard write policy applies - previewed under writeMode dry-run (nothing is sent), blocked under deny, sent under allow. Move mode is not destructive to the source file itself (only its documents relocate), so no destructive confirmation is needed beyond the standard write policy.

The source file itself always stays in place - a move leaves it empty, a copy leaves it untouched. Unlike F12 (merge), nothing is deleted.

notes: The file lookup must resolve to at most one file; more than one match is an error (IR-4001). No match is an error (IR-4001) unless forceCreate is true, in which case the file is created first (steps 3 and 4).

Documents always live under a folder, never directly in a file. The folder is found inside the file by its description (folderName); more than one match is an error (IR-4001). No match is an error (IR-4001) unless forceCreate is true, in which case the folder is created first (steps 6 and 7). On a newly created file the folder is always missing, so it is created too.

Validation needed - identifying the folder type by name (folderTypeName) is the owner's assumption and must be confirmed on a test server. Its id comes from the file's allowed types (GET /api/containers/{objectId}/allowedtypes), which list folder and document types together; which field (ClassId, Name) singles out a folder type by name is unconfirmed. On the folder-creation path folderTypeName is asked for when missing (needs-input) before anything is written.
Validation needed - Description on POST /api/folders/find is assumed to be an exact match on the folder description; the server-side semantics are unconfirmed.

On the file-creation path drawerCode is required (a missing one is rejected as needs-input) and createdByApplication is asked for when missing (needs-input); both checks happen before anything is written.
The file type code defaults to the drawer code, because drawer code and file type code are usually the same in the owner's setup; fileTypeCode overrides it.

Drawers have no separate code field; the drawer code is assumed to be the drawer's Name, as in F9. When the file exists, the drawer check compares its DrawerId with the drawer's Id; a mismatch is an error (IR-4107).
Validation needed - which object type field holds a document or file type code is unconfirmed; it must be checked on a test server. An unknown code is an error (IR-4006) naming the code.
Validation needed - document and folder Attributes are out of scope for this flow, and some document or folder types may mandate attributes; this must be checked against a test server.
The file is created with IsTemporary false. FileNumberPart2 and FileNumberPart3 are never sent.

Steps 4 (create file), 7 (create folder) and 9 (create document) are writes, so the standard write policy applies - previewed under writeMode dry-run (nothing is sent), blocked under deny, sent under allow. None is destructive, so no extra confirmation is needed beyond the standard write policy.
The create call returns the new document id (int64), which is the flow's output.

The file is found by its number and, when a drawer code is given, checked to sit in that drawer; the folder is found in that file by its description. Optionally the file and the folder are created first when they do not exist. The document type code is turned into its id before the document is created.

notes: The file lookup must resolve to at most one file; more than one match is an error (IR-4001). No match is an error (IR-4001) unless forceCreate is true (the default), in which case the file is created first (steps 3 and 4).

Documents always live under a folder, never directly in a file. The folder is found inside the file by its description, which in the owner's setup equals the folder type name (folderTypeName); more than one match is an error (IR-4001). No match is an error (IR-4001) unless forceCreate is true, in which case the folder is created first (steps 6 and 7) with folderTypeName as both its type and its description. On a newly created file the folder is always missing, so it is created too.

Validation needed - identifying the folder type by name (folderTypeName) is the owner's assumption and must be confirmed on a test server. Its id comes from the file's allowed types (GET /api/containers/{objectId}/allowedtypes), which list folder and document types together; which field (ClassId, Name) singles out a folder type by name is unconfirmed.
Validation needed - Description on POST /api/folders/find is assumed to be an exact match on the folder description; the server-side semantics are unconfirmed.

On the file-creation path the file type code is the drawer code (drawer code and file type code are usually the same in the owner's setup), the file Name is empty, IsTemporary is false, and createdByApplication is asked for when missing (needs-input) before anything is written. FileNumberPart2 and FileNumberPart3 are never sent.

Drawers have no separate code field; the drawer code is assumed to be the drawer's Name, as in F9. When the file exists, the drawer check compares its DrawerId with the drawer's Id; a mismatch is an error (IR-4107).
Validation needed - which object type field holds a document or file type code is unconfirmed; it must be checked on a test server. An unknown code is an error (IR-4006) naming the code.
Validation needed - document and folder Attributes are out of scope for this flow, and some document or folder types may mandate attributes; this must be checked against a test server.

Implementation note - splitting the PDF is local processing, not an API call, and the flow format has one API operation per step, so the split is folded into the page-upload step (step 11) rather than being a step of its own. Phase 2 renders each PDF page to an image, in page order, with a PDF library before the first upload.
The capture batch is opened with Application WebSdk, the same default as F3.
If a page upload fails midway, the document holds the pages uploaded so far (as in F3); the flow reports which pages succeeded and which failed, and phase 2 decides on cleanup.

Outputs - pageIds collects the Id of each created page, in page order; pageCount is the number of pages uploaded (the number of pages in the PDF on success). The page count comes from the local split, not from an API response, so it is not a step output.

Steps 4 (create file), 7 (create folder), 9 (create document), 10 (open batch) and 11 (upload pages) are writes, so the standard write policy applies - previewed under writeMode dry-run (nothing is sent), blocked under deny, sent under allow. None is destructive, so no extra confirmation is needed beyond the standard write policy.
F16.purpose: End-to-end document upload - resolve or create the file, the folder and the document, then split a local PDF into page images and upload each page. The file is found by its number and checked to sit in the given drawer; the folder is found in that file by its folder type name. With forceCreate (the default) a missing file and a missing folder are created first.
